title: Privilege tagging and evidence extraction hackbook — Q1 2026
content:
Purpose:
A concise, pragmatic hackbook for running quarterly least-privilege recertification cycles with minimal manual toil. Focus is on: (1) reliable entitlement tagging for RBAC v2 resources, (2) automated evidence extraction patterns, (3) SIEM export shape and sanity checks, and (4) practical remediation handoffs. This is a working doc — notes, commands, and TODOs are intentionally informal.

Scope: 
- Applies to: cloud console roles, internal service accounts, GitHub org/team privileges, and dedicated infra roles (Dedicated clusters, billing groups).
- Out of scope: user onboarding/offboarding playbook (separate doc), full attestation UI work.

Quick goals for Q1 2026 recert:
- Reduce human verification time by ~40% via automated evidence bundles.
- Ensure RBAC v2 mapping covers: role templates, composite roles, ephemeral grants, and external-idp groups.
- Produce 1 canonical SIEM export (CSV + JSONL) for auditors with field-level definitions.

Key constraints / assumptions:
- RBAC v2 is deployed company-wide; resource registry exists but incomplete (we will patch with heuristics).
- Not all services emit consistent audit logs; fallbacks: cloud API query + last-known-config snapshot.

High-level workflow (operational):
1) Entitlement inventory refresh (nightly job): run entitlement-collector to enumerate roles and bindings across all platforms. Output: inventory_{date}.jsonl in S3.
2) Tagging pass: apply deterministic tags (owner, resource_type, sensitivity, review_window) using tagger heuristics + manual overrides csv.
3) Evidence collection: for each principal->role mapping build an evidence bundle: recent audit events, last config diff, recent usage metrics (if available), and manager attestation link.
4) SIEM export and packing: transform bundles into auditor-friendly CSV + compressed JSONL; push to secure bucket and notify compliance leads.
5) Remediation loop: generate remediation tickets (JIRA-SC) with suggested actions and pre-filled repro steps.

Entitlement-tagging heuristics (examples):
- Owner: prefer explicit owner metadata, else map from resource path (e.g., /apps/checkout/* -> payments-team).
- Sensitivity: mark as high if resource path includes "prod" AND role in [admin, owner, billing].
- Review_window: 90 days default, 30 days for high sensitivity, 180 for read-only machine roles.
- Ephemeral: detect "ttl" or "expires_at" fields in bindings; tag as "ephemeral:true".

RBAC v2 edge cases to watch:
- Composite roles: role A includes role B; recert UI must surface effective permissions, not just direct bindings. Evidence extraction needs to expand composites into flat permission lists.
- External groups: Some idps (okta/google) report group names without a stable id; capture provider id and snapshot members at collection time.
- Service accounts with impersonation: collect both SA bindings and any principals allowed to impersonate the SA.
- Temporary escalation (just-in-time): include request logs from approval service; if absent, mark as "no-just-in-time-evidence".

Evidence bundle format (canonical fields):
- principal_id
- principal_type (user|service|group)
- resource_id
- role_id
- effective_permissions (comma-separated)
- last_used_ts (ISO8601 or null)
- recent_audit_events (array-encoded JSON string with max 20 events)
- config_snapshot_ts
- tags (comma-separated)
- attestation_link (URL or null)
Note: SIEM CSV will flatten recent_audit_events to a brief summary field (e.g., "last_event:read,ts:2026-02-12T11:02Z").

Sample SIEM mapping (fields -> expected types/examples):
- timestamp: string (ISO8601)
- actor_id: string (e.g., user:uid123)
- actor_type: string
- action: string (grant|revoke|assume|impersonate)
- target_resource: string
- target_role: string
- request_id: string
- source_ip: string or "-"
- proto: string (console|api|ssh)
- context: json_blob (minimized string)
Sanity checks: ensure timestamps are present and within collection window; drop events older than 365 days for recert bundles.

Automation playbook snippets (command-ish notes):
- Entitlement collector run: python tools/entitlement_collector.py --since 2026-01-01 --out s3://redwood-recert/inventory_20260101.jsonl
- Expand composites: python tools/role_expander.py --inventory inventory.jsonl --out expanded.jsonl --max-depth 5
- Evidence packer: bash scripts/pack_evidence.sh expanded.jsonl /tmp/bundles/ --siem-csv /tmp/siem/q1_2026.csv
- Quick local check: jq -r '.effective_permissions | join(",")' bundle.jsonl | head

Common manual checks (for reviewers):
- Confirm owner is correct and reachable (manager + on-call aliases).
- For high-sensitivity grants, ensure there is a documented business need in the last 180 days.
- For service accounts, validate last_used_ts vs expected worker cadence (e.g., batch job daily).
- If last_used_ts is null, add "no-usage-evidence" tag and route for deeper investigation.

Remediation templates (to pre-populate tickets):
- Suggested action: Remove direct admin role; replace with scoped role X and create time-bound approval for remainder.
- Evidence: include bundle S3 path, sample audit lines, and role expansion output.
- Priority: P1 for high-sensitivity active user grants; P2 for stale service accounts; P3 read-only grants older than 1 year.

Open questions / blockers (triage list):
- How to standardize "last_used" across services that only report activity logs for certain APIs? (Action: define fallbacks per provider)
- Need a compact format for recent_audit_events that is both human-readable and parsable by auditors. Current JSONL is too verbose. (Action: propose 3-line summary format).
- Who owns the manual override CSV? (suggestion: infra-product for infra roles, apps-owners for app-level roles).

Audit timeline (proposed sprint-aligned plan):
- Week -3: Inventory & tagger run, catch obvious gaps.
- Week -2: Evidence packer and SIEM export dry-run; produce sample CSV for compliance to vet.
- Week -1: Notifications to reviewers + short triage window.
- Week 0: Formal recertification deadline, automated ticket generation for unresolved items.
- Week +1 to +3: Remediation and verification.

Post-mortem metrics to capture:
- % of bindings with automated evidence (target 80%)
- Average human review time per item (target < 2 minutes)
- Number of false positives due to tagger heuristics (target < 5% of items reviewed)

Appendix: quick heuristics and regexes to identify prod vs staging resources:
- prod regexes: ".*/prod(/|$)|.*-prod(-|$)|projects/.*/prod-.*"
- staging regexes: "staging|qa|sandbox"

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Wire up an artifact that maps OKTA group stable id -> group name snapshot (Liam).
- Add a lightweight UI in recert console to show expanded effective permissions (Marina owns prototype).
- Draft auditor-friendly readme that explains why last_used may be empty for some infra roles.

If you are reading this and have an itch to hack: start with tools/role_expander — most of the downstream value (evidence, SIEM shape) comes from an accurate effective permission list.
